newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Caracas stocks end off, dragged by Electricdad.
newsitem.headline: Caracas stocks end off, dragged by Electricdad.

text.p: Caracas stocks closed off in slow trade, dragged down by profit-taking in leading utility Electricidad de Caracas, traders said.
"The stock's risen well recently, pushing along the rest of the market," said Banesco broker Simon Brad. "But today it fell, bringing down the rest," he added.

The bolsa's 19-share index closed off 0.86 percent at 6,639.16 points as 25 million shares traded worth three billion bolivars ($6.4 million) -- below the market's current $10 million average daily turnover.
Among traded stocks, 21 fell, 12 rose and nine closed flat, with telephone company CANTV among the gainers, rising 21 bolivars to end at 2091.00. Electricidad shed 8.00 bolivars, finishing at 529.00.

"It seems like the second half of Agenda Venezuela has stalled," said one trader. "There's not much good news -- electricity tariff adjustments have been delayed, there's the doctors' strike, and on-going problems with Viasa."
Sivensa stock also adjusted on a share dividend, ended at 161.40 bolivars after Friday's 326.00 close.
